extracted.intended_audience: novelists, creative-writing students, literary critics and readers interested in the craft and form of the novel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for choosing a novel’s subject and shaping its form — unity, scale, point of view, use of material, representation of time and space, and avoiding common compositional faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelist's eye for a subject (subject selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: How a novelist finds his subject, in a human being or in a situation or in a turn of thought...we judge the novelist’s eye for a subject to be his cardinal gift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The discovery of a fruitful idea is largely mysterious and not directly teachable; once the subject is announced the novelist becomes accessible and the reader may follow and judge the treatment. Example/implication: Tolstoy found an 'unwritten book' in the world that others would not detect; the selection of subject is the foundational creative act and is decisive for subsequent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form must coincide with the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: The best form is that which makes the most of its subject—there is no other definition of the meaning of form in fiction...the form of the book depends on it, and until it is known there is nothing to be said of the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the book’s formal design expresses the subject fully: where form and subject diverge, material is superfluous or lacking and the story suffers. Anti-pattern: a pleasing set of parts that do not cohere into a form expressing the subject (as argued of War and Peace).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject unity and expressibility (put subject in a phrase)
rubrics_metrics.description: A subject is anyhow expressible in ten words that reveal its unity. If it cannot be put into a phrase it is no subject for a novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before judging form, identify the novel’s subject in a concise phrase; use that phrase as the organizing principle for structure and selection. If a reader cannot summarize the subject, the novel risks lacking a coherent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative coherence: treatment must follow the true development of the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: From point to point we follow the writer, always looking back to the subject itself in order to understand the logic of the course he pursues...Is this proceeding of the author the right one, the best for the subject? Is it possible to conceive and to name a better?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At each narrative turn ask whether the author’s choice advances the subject or contradicts it. The reader ‘recreates’ the author's labour and judges whether individual episodes and turns are true to the subject’s development; deviations indicate flaws in treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid multiple conflicting designs (unity/focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: A confusion of two designs...It has no centre, and Tolstoy is so clearly unconcerned by the lack that one must conclude he never perceived it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let the novel contain two large, independently treated themes that fail to merge (anti-pattern: 'two novels at once'). If two themes are present they must be subordinated or unified by a central organizing idea; otherwise the whole will lack a centre and coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate scale, population and scope to express the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Such a subject could not be treated at all without a generous amount of room for its needs...It requires, to begin with, a big and various population; a few selected figures may hold the main thread but a wide world must be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the novel’s physical and temporal scale, number of characters, and breadth of world to the demands of the subject. If the subject is expansive (march of generations, national saga) provide ample scope; if it is inward, a narrower horizon may be more appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view consistency and management of narrative authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes Tolstoy is immediately beside us, narrating; in the other it is Peter and Andrew...who are with us and about us, and Tolstoy is effaced...The predominant point of view is simply his own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether the narrative will primarily operate through an effaced viewpoint (characters’ consciousnesses) or an authoritative narrator, and maintain a consistent or purposefully varied method. Random shifts between narrator-as-author and character-centered perspective undermine unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid intrusive authorial commentary and didactic interruptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tolstoy is capable of thrusting into his book interminable chapters of comment and explanation, chapters in the manner of a controversial pamphlet, lest the argument of his drama should be missed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit overt theoretical digressions or polemical 'pamphleteering' that pull the reader out of the fictional world. Anti-pattern: long explanatory chapters that read like essays; readers may skip such passages and their presence weakens the novel’s narrative integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of indirectness and onlooker perspective to enhance effect
rubrics_metrics.description: He approaches it through the mind of an onlooker, borrowing the value of indirectness, the increased effect of a story that is seen as it is mirrored in the mind of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, present major events indirectly through the consciousness of a character or observer to deepen effect. Choose onlookers deliberately and maintain methodical selection rather than random choice; this indirectness can intensify emotional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of the passage of time (form of time)
rubrics_metrics.description: The passage of time...belongs to the heart of the subject...Merely to lengthen the series of stages and developments in the action will not ensure it; the form of time is to be represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do more than list chronologies or announce lapses of years; structure scenes, transitions, and pacing so that readers perceive the shape and effects of time. Use techniques (recurrent motifs, measured ellipses, shifts in perspective) that make the movement of time felt, not merely stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of material — avoid wastefulness; make full use of material
rubrics_metrics.description: War and Peace is wasteful of its subject; that is the whole objection to its loose, unstructural form...the well-made book is the book in which the subject and the form coincide and are indistinguishable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every scene, digression, and character serves the central subject or is deliberately subordinated; superfluous material dilutes impact and leaves the subject underdeveloped. Editing away interpolations often clarifies form and strengthens the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters should be representative and clearly situated in a wider world
rubrics_metrics.description: They are choice examples, standing away from the mass, but their meaning would be lost if they were taken to be utterly exceptional. Their attachment to the general drama of life must accordingly be felt and understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make characters typical enough to embody the subject’s concerns while anchoring them in a wider social or historical context. Avoid isolating characters in a self-contained 'world of their own' unless the fable requires such enclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of space and use of setting to support the novel’s motive
rubrics_metrics.description: The continuity of space and daylight...is rendered in War and Peace with absolute mastery...Dostoevsky needed no lucid prospect; all he sought was a blaze of light on the extraordinary theatre of their consciousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose setting and atmospheric treatment to serve the subject: an open, expansive world suits themes of breadth and representativeness; a narrowed, intense environment suits inward, psychological fables. Use description economically — setting can imply scope without exhaustive detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity of train-of-action for focused themes
rubrics_metrics.description: There remains a long succession of scenes, in a single and straightforward train of action...It is still a novel of ample size...At any rate, it is one theme and one book, and the question of its form may be further pressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the subject permits, prefer a single, coherent sequence of action that carries the reader from opening to climax; excise or relocate material that belongs to a different thematic design to preserve clarity of form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader engagement and the pleasure of creative re-creation
rubrics_metrics.description: The pleasure of creation is open to every reader, volume in hand...the hours of the author’s labour are lived again by the reader, the pleasure of creation is renewed...the book is recreated according to the best of the reader’s ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-formed novel invites active critical reading whereby the reader reconstructs the work’s design; fostering such engagement (through clear subject, consistent method, and evocative scenes) prolongs the book’s life and deepens its effect.
